why:
The join that turns a DISCOVERED node's two halves into one name: `/robot` + `talker` -> `/robot/talker`, with the root namespace collapsed so `/` + `talker` is `/talker` and never `//talker`.

Ours-only, and ROS 2's absence is structural rather than an oversight. `rcl_get_node_names` returns two PARALLEL owning arrays that the caller correlates by index and joins itself; rclcpp joins for you one layer up (`Node::get_node_names()` returns fully-qualified strings) and rclc has no graph API at all, so a C user there reaches rcl and joins by hand. `rcl_node_get_fully_qualified_name` exists but answers only for the CALLER'S OWN node — that one we mirror.

It exists here because of the constraint one row over: our enumeration is a VISITOR (no allocator at the seam, no caller-knowable bound on the graph), so both halves arrive together in one call and the join is the only step left. Three hand-rolled copies of it already existed in-tree and they did not agree on a namespace with no leading slash, which is what made this a named function rather than a fourth.
